Package com.signalwire.sdk.swml

Enum Class RecordDirection

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<RecordDirection>
com.signalwire.sdk.swml.RecordDirection
All Implemented Interfaces:
WireEnum, Serializable, Comparable<RecordDirection>, Constable
public enum RecordDirection extends Enum<RecordDirection> implements WireEnum
Audio direction for the SWML record_call verb, as a typed, compile-time-checked closed set.

The Python reference FunctionResult.record_call validates direction against ["speak", "listen", "both"] and raises ValueError on anything else. The methods that take a record direction (FunctionResult.recordCall(String, boolean, String, RecordDirection)) accept this enum or a plain String. The enum gives editor autocompletion and makes a typo fail at compile time (a bare string like "listenn" only fails at runtime, on the server). Strings keep parity with the Python reference (which uses a bare str): 


 result.recordCall("rec1", true, "mp3", RecordDirection.LISTEN);   // typed, autocompleted
 result.recordCall("rec1", true, "mp3", "listen");                 // string still works (parity)

This is a DIFFERENT set from TapDirection. record_call uses listen where tap uses hear, mirroring the reference's two separate validation lists — the two sets are modelled as two distinct enums and are never shared (see the 3-vocabulary trap: SWML record_call {speak,listen,both} vs SWML tap {speak,hear,both} vs RELAY {listen,speak,both}).

Each constant's value is the canonical wire string, so routing a recording through the enum is byte-for-byte identical to passing that string.

    • fromWire

      public static RecordDirection fromWire(String wire)
      Parse a wire string into a RecordDirection, or return null if it is not a recognised direction (the same strings the Python reference would reject with ValueError). Note "hear" is valid for TapDirection but NOT for record_call, so it returns null here. The Java analog of Rust's from_str.
      Parameters:
      wire - the candidate wire string (case-sensitive).
      Returns:
      the matching constant, or null if none matches.
